concerns.text: T031 implements a sensitivity analysis using a RandomForestClassifier and F1-score, whereas FR-005 and SC-003 explicitly mandate a sensitivity analysis on the regressor reporting RMSE variance. This task silently relaxes the requirement to analyze the continuous target relationship, violating the spec's core methodology.

T024a implements a one-sample t-test comparing 5 CV fold scores against a single scalar null RMSE. SC-002 requires a statistical test proving the model is distinguishable from the null model. Comparing a sample distribution to a constant without a null distribution (e.g., via bootstrap or paired test) is a semantic weakening of the statistical rigor required by the spec.

T012 caps the dataset at 10,000 rows but fails to implement the 'fail gracefully' acceptance scenario from spec.md (Edge Cases) for when the source returns <500 valid entries. The task assumes sufficient data exists, silently dropping the requirement to handle the empty/insufficient data case with a specific error.

T031 calculates the Coefficient of Variation (CV) of F1-scores and flags failure if CV > 0.10. SC-003 requires demonstrating that the metric varies by a negligible margin (absolute variance <10% or RMSE variance). Using relative variability (CV) as a proxy for absolute margin is a semantic relaxation of the acceptance criterion.

T029a (Collinearity Detection) is a prerequisite for the 'stable model' used in T028 and T031. The task description implies a retraining step if collinearity is found, but the spec (US-3) requires this check to verify stability. If T029a is not explicitly defined to produce a 'stable model' artifact that T028/T031 depend on, the subsequent tasks violate the constitution's requirement for robust generalization estimates.
